title: I Told My Sister I Would Not Be the Secret Childcare

parts.text: I said no to watching her kids and watched her call me selfish in the kitchen. I am twenty-six, designer, Saturday studio time, the only quiet I get. Leah treats my apartment like a free daycare with better snacks. The kids are fine. The assumption is not. She had a concert. I had a deadline. The fridge hummed like it wanted to leave too. I had leftover pasta in a cracked container, the one that never seals. I offered to help her find a sitter in the group chat, not my couch. She said blood is thicker. Blood does not render files. I sat with the no until it felt like furniture. She found a sitter. The concert happened. I hit the deadline. Sunday she brought donuts as a half apology. I ate one. I did not un-say no. The cracked pasta lid is still cracked. Boundaries can look like donuts and still be real. Leah said, "So you won't even do family" I said, "I won't be unpaid childcare on a deadline" The kids hugged me anyway. I hugged back. That was not a yes. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened.

social.video_title: I refused to be the last-minute concert sitter
social.description: Cracked pasta lid, fridge hum, a deadline. She found a sitter. I ate one donut. Would you have folded?
